diagram_math_checks.objects: S1, S2, S3 are successive point blowups over the same field; E1,E2,E3 are exceptional curves, primes denote subsequent strict transforms.
diagram_math_checks.check: The explanatory text retains AC and characteristic different from 2 and 3. Panels are explicitly incidence schematics, not pictures of k-points. Moving right denotes the construction, not a blowup morphism in the wrong direction.

diagram_math_checks.objects: First chart y=xt, Z1:x=t^2 and E1:x=0.
diagram_math_checks.check: Substitution into y^2-x^3 gives x^2(t^2-x). Removing the exceptional factor gives the plotted sideways parabola, tangent to x=0. The quotient k[x,t]/(x,t^2-x)=k[t]/(t^2) has one point of length two, as step 1.2 and the local intersection definition require. The single marked point therefore is not two reduced contacts.

Substitution yields y^2(1-ys^3). On its strict transform ys^3=1, so y and s are units; this lies in the chart overlap s invertible, with t=s^{-1}, and contributes no point above the cusp. This justifies not drawing an extra branch or exceptional intersection.

t^2-x=t(t-u), so Z2:t-u=0; x=tu gives E1 strict transform u=0 and new E2:t=0. Their pairwise ideals (u,t),(u,t-u),(t,t-u) all equal (t,u), so contacts have length one, but all three components meet: not SNC under F2 and def-strict-normal-crossings-divisor. This agrees with step 2.2.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Third exceptional curve E3 with E1 double-prime, Z3, E2 prime.
diagram_math_checks.check: The distinct tangent directions on S2 are [1:0], [1:1], [0:1] in coordinates [t:u]. Blowing up separates them into distinct points of E3; each branch is regular and meets E3 once transversely by the local chart calculation and the regular-source intersection-drop supplier. The panel shows disjoint strict transforms meeting E3 at three separate points, each with two components. This is step 3.1, not an SNC conclusion from normalization alone.
